purpose: Replay a stored drive's telemetry-enriched GPS trail with synchronized map, transport, current-position measurements and historical charts.
primaryGoal: Understand what happened along a drive and seek precisely between its route, elapsed-time timeline and elevation profile without losing stored totals or source trust.

dataSources.ownership: Drive detail handler composes the stored drive record and signal.StateReader historical telemetry/position timelines.
dataSources.queryBehavior: ['drive', id]; enabled only with an ID; forwards AbortSignal; polls INTERVALS.FAST only when data.live === true; otherwise inherits query policy.
dataSources.units: Stored summary uses distanceM, durationS, energyUsedWh, avgSpeedMps and maxSpeedMps. Position speed is projected from VehicleSpeed without a display conversion. Per-row power is explicitly computed as pack_voltage * pack_current / 1000 in the inspected backend and is currently kW, despite the application-wide SI mandate. Do not blindly divide it again or normalize the cache in a page redesign.
dataSources.limits: No network request exercised; StateReader implementation, sampling/completeness and real server response not verified. Elevation is explicitly absent from the telemetry projection because no current Fleet Telemetry Elevation atomic is emitted.

dataSources.ownership: Existing client playback clock; currentIndex is the shared cursor for all page surfaces.
dataSources.behavior: 20 fps virtual clock; speed slots 1/10/25/50/100; time-based seeking, relative seconds, frame stepping, play/pause/stop; timeline endpoint signature resets playback.

dataSources.endpoint: Transitive preference endpoints not traced in this bounded page audit
dataSources.ownership: Existing application formatting/settings and operational-metric owners.
dataSources.behavior: Preserve saved distance/speed/temperature, locale, raw SI summary values and numeric missing-state handling; conversions occur in display derivations, not wire/cache.

duplicatedPatterns.fix: Use one feature-owned pure derivation with identical missing-pair and rounding semantics; no speculative app-wide component.

issues.detail: Restart, play and stop explicitly use h-8 w-8; shortcut help at :474 uses h-7 w-7. These source sizes are below the contract's stronger 44px mobile default. Actual rendered sizes and any WCAG spacing exception are untested.
issues.fix: Existing shared transport owner should supply coarse-pointer/touch 44px targets while retaining compact visual glyphs, wrapping and transport behavior. Do not add a page-local transport.

existing: Named page map/timeline regions and localized refresh/back controls; decorative readout icons are aria-hidden.

issues.detail: The chart declares chart-a11y:no-table and does not pass data/dataColumns to ChartCard; TripReplayElevation.tsx:47 does the same. Stored totals/current readouts cannot convey the complete per-sample trends. Shared ChartContainer.tsx:171-186 already supports screen-reader/forced-colors fallback data.
issues.fix: Supply localized time/distance, speed, power and elevation columns via the existing ChartCard data/dataColumns contract, preserving nullable values and sample indices. Use existing scrubber keyboard seeking; do not invent another chart engine.

issues.detail: Speed categories and start/end route pins use color alone in the inspected map renderer, with no textual speed-band legend or start/end labels in this component. Current readouts and keyboard transport exist but do not explain the route colors.
issues.fix: Add restrained localized textual route key/start-end context using existing map/UI composition, with explicit unknown-speed category; retain route-click seeking and keyboard transport. Verify real Leaflet semantics before claiming a complete accessibility failure/pass.

states.loading: Page derives historical DataState and passes loading=status initial to PageLayout (:117-118,413-416); PageContainer.tsx:243-244 renders the canonical skeleton instead of children.
states.fatalError: Only fatalError is forwarded as page error; header refresh/back remain configured. PageContainer.tsx:245-246 uses ErrorDisplay.
states.retainedErrorOffline: deriveDataState.ts:158-177 retains payload for refresh errors/paused fetching. Page retains map/charts; TripOperationalBrief.tsx:25-31 exposes source freshness/provenance and status. PageContainer query prop also supplies DataFreshnessAuto.
states.emptyGps: Page :451-460 shows an explanatory GPS-empty panel and retains stored summary totals. Playback/map/elevation/timeline are currently absent when no usable positions exist; retain this existing branch semantics unless explicit product/integration change is assigned.
states.missingMetrics: SOC NaN is deliberately distinct from zero; other nullable readouts use em dash. Elevation preserves null gaps and has an unavailable EmptyState. Speed/power chart shows EmptyState only when both series lack observations.
states.stationaryGps: TripReplayMap.tsx:145-159 and :317-331 keep anchor location and explain why no route can be drawn.

issues.detail: The speed sparkline converts null speed to 0 in both full and downsampled branches (:355,361), visually representing unknown speed as a measured stop.
issues.fix: Preserve missing samples as gaps using the existing chart owner if supported; otherwise omit only the decorative sparkline when incomplete while keeping primary nullable timeline series and every replay sample.

issues.detail: nearestTelemetry always returns the nearest row without a maximum timestamp distance or per-measurement evidence. Widely separated observations can be presented as current SOC/power/range/temp at a GPS sample.
issues.fix: Define a typed feature join with explicit temporal provenance/availability, and validate permissible matching against source semantics before selecting a tolerance. Do not invent a two-minute rule for historical telemetry or silently interpolate.

issues.detail: Missing latitude/longitude become 0 and only the pair (0,0) is filtered at :198. A row with one missing coordinate therefore survives as a fabricated point, affecting route, distance and nearest-sample seeking.
issues.fix: Validate each coordinate independently as finite and within geographic bounds before including a point; retain actual valid zero latitude/longitude and expose unavailable counts rather than inventing coordinates.

visualIssues.detail: Decorative scrubber sparkline pins cyan #22d3ee and active readout highlight at :376 pins a cyan ring. The map and elevation/cursor renderers also pin saturated hex colors independently of canonical palettes.
visualIssues.fix: Use existing palette/semantic tokens and a subdued event outline; keep selected series/theme preferences, event meaning, route visibility and playhead position. Tone down decoration rather than removing measurement series.

visualIssues.detail: Elevation uses a fixed emerald fill with explicit 0.4 gradient opacity and fixed stroke at :90; speed/power reference cursor pins #00b4d8 at TripReplayCharts.tsx:196. These bypass the otherwise shared chart palette.
visualIssues.fix: Adopt existing chart palette/reference tokens with restrained area opacity while preserving measured/null samples, axis units, exports, cursor and legend state.

architectureIssues.detail: speedColor(kmh) uses thresholds 30/60/100, but :178 passes raw curr.speed from the page's SI-normalized positions. The backend projects VehicleSpeed directly to speed. The map therefore compares m/s values with km/h thresholds.
architectureIssues.fix: Keep raw SI positions/cache and translate the existing documented physical category thresholds to SI inside the feature derivation (or convert only this classification input at its display boundary). Add boundary/null cases and avoid dependence on viewer speed units.

architectureIssues.detail: restoredRef is mount-scoped, not drive-ID-scoped; restoration effect depends only on positions.length (:248). A same-component route-ID transition can retain true and fail to restore the new drive's at/play parameters even though useTripReplay resets its timeline.
architectureIssues.fix: Key restoration and debounce lifecycle to the drive ID/query identity, preserving unrelated search params, valid 0..1 bounds, 300ms replace writes and requested autoplay. Test same-instance drive changes, including equal sample counts.

architectureIssues.detail: Marker labels ('Start', 'End', 'Fast segment', 'Regen peak', 'Battery <20%', clustered labels) are hardcoded in the pure helper and copied into the scrubber at TripReplayPage.tsx:218-223; surrounding page labels are localized.
architectureIssues.fix: Keep marker algorithms/ordering/counts intact and translate structured marker kind/count/threshold metadata at the existing presentation boundary; avoid importing i18n into a pure algorithm or adding a second catalog.

architectureIssues.detail: A continuous negative battery-power interval is labeled Charge start/stop after 30 seconds, while the page's power help describes negative power as regenerative braking. Power sign alone does not establish an actual charge session.
architectureIssues.fix: Preserve existing event detection for modernization; separately have the domain owner confirm event semantics and supply authoritative charge evidence or accurate regen labels. Do not invent session data or delete marker families as a visual fix.

competingImplementations.detail: Feature chart components already forward children through ChartCard -> EmbeddedChart -> ChartContainer. Missing accessible data is caller adoption, not a reason for a new chart/table pipeline.
OperationalBrief owns eight stored/derived summary metrics; TripReplayReadout owns six cursor-local measurements. Different scopes; do not collapse either into a replacement KPI grid.
PlaybackControls/TimelineScrubber and useTripReplay already separate rendering from clock/state. Do not introduce a second replay controller or shortcut engine.

data: Raw SI stored summary values and saved display/locale preferences remain unchanged; existing per-row kW backend exception must not be silently corrected by a page-only modernization.
Drive summary survives missing GPS; nearest-by-time telemetry enrichment and position-first field precedence are existing behavior requiring explicit trust review before algorithm changes.
Single replay.currentIndex synchronizes map, elevation cursor, speed/power cursor, current readouts and transport.
Null metric/elevation gaps remain distinct from measured zero; SOC NaN sentinel remains unavailable rather than 0%.
Cumulative route distance is haversine-derived; elevation totals count only consecutive measured pairs; efficiency remains energy/distance with positive-distance prerequisite.
Retained refresh-error/paused payloads remain visible; only initial fatal failures replace content.
Stationary GPS retains anchor location and explanatory banner; no invented elevation signal or route data.
Query key, AbortSignal forwarding, live-only polling, mutation/auth boundaries and workspace-owned selectors are unchanged.
